Global Engagement Map – A Global University Skip to content All the UW Current site Search scope All the UW Current site Enter search text MyUW Calendar Directories Libraries UW Medicine Maps UW News Helpful Links Information Technology Workday HCM Husky Card UW Bothell UW Tacoma UW Facebook UW Twitter University of Washington University of Washington UW Global Quick Links Menu Home About Global Learning in Our Colleges and Schools Global Partnerships Global Engagement Map UW Global UW Global Travel UW Study Abroad Make a gift Global Engagement Map A Global University Global Engagement Map Welcome to the University of Washington’s interactive global engagement map! Explore our international connections through four key areas: international students, study abroad, alumni, and collaborative research. Click on the tabs to visualize data, hover over countries for insights, and search for specific nations to learn more. Map Key Data Sources Using the Map Learn More International students This visualization shows the number of UW international students by country of origin during the last completed academic year. Students with UW-sponsored visas are included in this map. Study abroad This visualization shows the number of students who studied abroad in each country during the last completed academic year. Alumni This visualization shows UW alumni living in each country outside the U.S. This is a complete set of all alumni. Research and publications This visualization shows global engagement and collaboration in research. It represents the following two datasets: Research publications with a co-author at an institution outside the United States, identified using open source data from the Microsoft Academic Graph . Research awards with an international component, as identified by the investigator in UW SAGE . At the time of proposal, the investigator indicated on the eGC1 that project work will be performed internationally and selected a related country. Funds were not necessarily spent internationally. In the future, we hope to provide more detailed information about individual projects and publications, as well as faculty affiliations. Partners from across the University worked together to make this project possible, including the Office of Global Affairs , UW Information Technology – Enterprise Data Services , Office of Planning & Budgeting – Institutional Analysis , University Advancement and the Office of Research . The publications data in the research and publications visualization is powered by OpenAlex . Institutional data comes from the UW Information Technology – Enterprise Data Warehouse (EDW) . The four visualizations represent global trends in the following areas: International students, study abroad, alumni, and research and publications. Click on a button above the map to view a particular visualization. Hover over a country to learn more. To learn about a particular country in detail, type the name of any country into the search bar at the top left. Hover over the icon to read stories or learn about alumni communities. Grants Management for Investigators (GMI) Human Subjects Division Training and Education Required Research Training Home Required Training Grants Management for Investigators Grants Management for Investigators Course Description The Grants Management for Investigators (GMI) orientation and refresher provide an overview of the grants management process at the University of Washington, including processes, compliance requirements, and audit concerns at each stage of the research project lifecycle. The focus is on PI roles and responsibilities for administering sponsored agreements and on the role of central offices at the UW in supporting processes and compliance for those agreements. Who is required to take this training? All University of Washington principal investigators (faculty and non-faculty) who apply for or receive externally funded grants or contracts are required to attend the 2 hour orientation initially with a 40 minute on-demand refresher every four years thereafter. (More frequent attendance is encouraged to remain current with significant changes in sponsored program policy.) This opportunity is open to all eligible persons regardless of race, sex or other identity . Summary of the requirement The Office of the Provost requires GMI training of all UW faculty members and non-faculty principal investigators who receive externally funded grants or contracts to cover the management of research activities which occur under increasingly complex regulations by funding agencies, and federal and state governments. Grants Management for Investigators Orientation Requirement (2 hours) Audience: New principal investigators and non-PIs actively seeking funding, who have yet to attend a Grants Management for Investigators orientation. Faculty and non-faculty who submit a proposal as UW Principal Investigator for the first time must attend a live or recorded orientation within twelve months of submitting the proposal via SAGE, if they have not attended one previously. First-time PIs are strongly encouraged to attend a orientation before submitting the proposal. The live orientation is offered once per year via Zoom in the fall. The fall presentation for 2025 has occurred; this session will become available as an on-demand offering soon. Through the rest of the year, PIs can meet their attendance requirement by viewing the recorded orientation. Grants Management for Investigators Online Refresher (45 minutes) Audience: Principal investigators who have previously attended an in-person orientation. After the initial attendance at an in-person orientation, all principal investigators are required to renew their training every four years by completing the online refresher. The on-demand refresher highlights compliance requirements, new federal and state regulations, and recent changes to research infrastructure and policy. The material is organized into required and optional modules; the entire course will take no more than forty-five minutes. Receiving Course Credit Completion records for the online options are downloaded from the learning management system monthly and manually loaded into MyResearch Training Transcript. It can take up to a month for your GMI completion record to show up in MRTT.
